finding.claim: Missing await on async authorize() in DELETE /reports/:id. The 403 rejection is never observed, so the delete always proceeds. Any caller who reaches the handler can delete any report regardless of grants. The rejected promise is also unhandled, which can crash the process on newer Node versions.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (or any request, if the session is absent) sends DELETE /reports/:id with an arbitrary id.

trace.note: DELETE handler entry, id taken from req.params.id
report loaded by id with no ownership scoping
authorize() called without await or return. The async function returns a promise, the throw becomes a rejection, and execution continues
authorize() is async and signals denial only by throwing, so the un-awaited call enforces nothing

finding.guards_checked: authorize() itself is correct, but its result is discarded at line 20. The PUT handler at line 27 awaits it correctly, which is the sibling comparison. No other middleware performs authorization. The middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user. No other guard was found on this route.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 error on denial, but the call at line 20 is a bare statement with no await, return, or catch, so nothing enforces it. The middleware at lines 4-7 only copies the session user. No other guard exists.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() without await, so its throw at line 14 becomes an unobserved rejection and db.reports.remove at line 21 runs regardless. The PUT route at line 27 awaits it correctly, so any authenticated low-privilege user can delete any report. The "anonymous" part of the claim is slightly overstated, since line 5 would throw on a missing session, but that doesn't change the verdict.
